questions.q: In the fulfillment-order case study scenario, why does deciding the Fulfillment_Order__c to Opportunity relationship (lookup vs. master-detail) require the same reasoning taught in Lesson 12?
options: Because the relationship type should be chosen randomly for case studies
Because Salesforce does not allow master-detail relationships on custom objects created after 2020
Because lookup relationships are always correct for financial data

Because the right choice depends on what should happen to the Fulfillment_Order__c record if the Opportunity needs to be deleted and recreated during data cleanup — the same 'what happens on delete' question Lesson 12 taught
questions.explain: Lesson 12 taught that the real question behind lookup vs. master-detail is what should happen to the child record on parent deletion — the same reasoning applies directly to deciding Fulfillment_Order__c's relationship to Opportunity in this case study.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say the integration design for the fulfillment scenario might reasonably use two different patterns for its two directions?
options: Because Salesforce requires every integration to use exactly one pattern regardless of direction

Because outbound (Salesforce to WMS) and inbound (WMS to Salesforce) traffic can have different real requirements, and Lesson 13 taught that pattern choice should be driven by the actual business need in each direction, not a single blanket choice
Because using two patterns is always a documentation mistake that should be flagged in review
Because the WMS cannot support more than one integration pattern simultaneously
questions.explain: Lesson 13 taught that pattern choice (request-reply, fire-and-forget, batch, event-driven) should fit the actual need — the two directions of this integration can reasonably have different needs and therefore different pattern choices.

questions.q: What does this lesson say a 'mock review session' should test, beyond simply rereading the documentation for completeness?
options: Whether the document uses correct grammar and spelling
Whether the document is exactly the length specified by the template

Whether the documentation set can answer pointed, skeptical questions using only what's already written, which exposes places where a decision was never actually worked through rather than just under-described
Whether the document has been approved by Salesforce support
questions.explain: A mock review session's value is testing whether the documentation holds up to pointed questions using only its own written content — a gap exposed this way usually means a decision was never actually made, not just poorly written down.

questions.q: Which three recurring gaps does this lesson specifically call out as common even after completing the rest of this course?
options: Using the wrong diagramming tool, missing a legend, and forgetting a version stamp
Writing too many ADRs, over-documenting the data model, and including too many diagrams
Skipping the system context diagram, omitting the access matrix, and using the wrong notation style
Stating a relationship choice without its reasoning, treating integration error handling as an afterthought, and an executive summary that hides a real trade-off
questions.explain: The lesson specifically names these three recurring first-attempt gaps: omitting the 'why' behind a relationship choice, under-treating error handling in an integration section, and softening or hiding a real trade-off in an executive summary.

questions.q: If a mock review question exposes a place in the case study documentation that can't be answered from what's already written, what does this lesson say that means?
options: That specific gap is a real gap in the design's reasoning, not just a writing problem — it should be noted and the relevant section fixed
The mock review exercise itself was flawed and should be discarded
It means the question was unfair and outside the scope of the scenario
It means the entire documentation set must be rewritten from scratch
questions.explain: The lesson frames an unanswerable question as exactly the kind of real gap this course exists to surface before a real review board, audit, or production incident finds it — the fix is targeted (update the relevant section), not a full rewrite.
